title: How a validated explanation reaches a learner
subtitle: A focused training fixture covering evidence, rendering, interaction, and review.

audience.participationGoal: Review an explanation pack and identify the correct layer for a safe improvement

sourceScope.summary: The skill designs the lesson, the validator checks its contract, and the renderer presents it without executing source content.

sources.label: Understanding Pack skill
sources.evidence: Defines profile selection, evidence collection, visual design, and browser proof.

sources.label: Output contract
sources.evidence: Defines decision and training shapes, density limits, quiz evidence, and source links.

sources.label: Renderer
sources.evidence: Escapes authored data and renders distinct visuals, navigation, and quiz feedback.

visuals.title: Three layers, three responsibilities
visuals.teachingGoal: Map each concern to the layer that owns it.

items.label: Skill
items.detail: Selects the reader, profile, evidence, and teaching strategy.

items.label: Validator
items.detail: Rejects broken structure, source links, excessive length, and invalid quiz targets.

items.label: Renderer
items.detail: Turns trusted data into a responsive visual document with bounded local interaction.

learningObjectives: Explain the separate jobs of the skill, validator, and renderer
Choose the correct layer for a teaching or presentation change
Verify that quiz feedback returns a learner to supporting evidence

background.title: JSON is the reviewable source
background.body: Authored content and evidence live in structured data; the HTML shell is deterministic output.

intuition.essence: The skill chooses what to teach, validation protects the agreement, and rendering makes relationships visible.

example.input: An owner asks whether a protocol PR is safe to approve.
example.result: The skill selects a concise decision brief with approval evidence instead of a full employee course.
example.why: Matching the artifact to the next job removes repetition while preserving traceability.

walkthrough.title: Choose the reader's next job
walkthrough.explanation: Approval selects a decision brief; onboarding or operational learning selects a training pack.
walkthrough.consequence: The artifact no longer forces identical sections on owners and employees.
checkpoints: Name the decision or operation before drafting

walkthrough.title: Connect each claim to evidence
walkthrough.whyNow: A concise artifact still needs defensible claims.
walkthrough.explanation: Current behavior, proposals, inferences, and unknowns receive explicit labels and source references.
walkthrough.consequence: The reader can challenge a claim without searching the entire repository.
checkpoints: Do not turn missing proof into confident prose

walkthrough.title: Render distinct visual forms and exercise them
walkthrough.explanation: The renderer uses separate flow, comparison, timeline, mapping, and guided-step layouts, then browser checks confirm their controls.
walkthrough.consequence: A tabbed text inventory can no longer masquerade as every kind of figure.
checkpoints: Check incomplete, correct, incorrect, and reset quiz states

edgeCases.scenario: A quiz cites evidence but links to no teaching passage
edgeCases.behavior: Validation rejects the missing review target.
edgeCases.why: Feedback should return the learner to the explanation that supports the answer.

quiz.instructions: Answer all three questions. Checking marks the correct choice, explains it, and links back to the relevant passage.

questions.prompt: Which profile fits an owner deciding whether to approve one PR?
questions.supportingClaim: An approval decision uses the decision-brief profile.

options.label: Decision brief
options.rationale: Correct. It leads with the decision, proof, risks, and open questions.

options.label: Training pack
options.rationale: Training is for operating, onboarding, or teaching the workflow.

options.label: Guided mode
options.rationale: Guided is an evidence mode, not the output profile.

options.label: Raw source map
options.rationale: Traceability supports the brief but does not replace the explanation.

questions.prompt: Where should a contributor change how a flow is visually drawn?
questions.supportingClaim: Presentation behavior belongs to the deterministic renderer.

options.label: In the renderer
options.rationale: Correct. The renderer owns trusted markup and interaction.

options.label: In source evidence
options.rationale: Evidence describes behavior; it does not own presentation.

options.label: In the quiz answer
options.rationale: Quiz content tests the model but does not draw diagrams.

questions.prompt: What should happen when a learner has answered only two of three questions?
questions.supportingClaim: Incomplete quizzes reveal no answers and keep checking disabled.

options.label: Show the correct answers immediately
options.rationale: That compromises retrieval practice before the learner commits.

options.label: Score the answered subset
options.rationale: A partial score changes the meaning of the check.

options.label: Keep checking disabled and reveal nothing
options.rationale: Correct. Feedback appears only after every selection exists.

options.label: Submit the result to the server
options.rationale: The artifact stores and transmits no quiz results.

limitations: This fixture verifies the local artifact shell, not every browser version used by employees.
